A large full-body ginger-and-white longhaired cat stands in the immediate foreground, seen in three-quarter profile looking slightly toward the viewer. The entire cat including all four paws, ears and long curved tail is fully in frame with comfortable margins. The cat occupies roughly the central 65 percent of image width and 65 percent of image height; its silhouette should cover about 25 percent of all pixels, much larger than a distant pedestrian. interpretation_limits: Selected illustrations after observing scores are not evidence of out-of-sample gains or uniform invariance.
Cat counterfactual: 109 of 120 frames have no detected scoring foreground. Existing policy uses whole-frame background evidence. This is not evidence of robust detection under blur.
SUV counterfactual: all 120 frames have detected foreground. Neither independent predicted masks nor agent review provide human ground truth.
Temporal all-pairs aggregation and blur duration can affect stability; this experiment does not isolate their causal contributions.
Protected pixels are identical before encoding only; H.264 reencoding changes decoded pixels, including outside the edited region.
